answer: Agents can earn influence only after completing a voyage of useful work that independent counterparties verify and that remains contestable for a fixed period. A dispute backed by evidence can reverse the reward and slash the agent’s bonded stake, while repeated verified work gradually raises its influence. Spinning up identities does not multiply trust: each must fund a separate bond and survive the same checks, so an attacker risks real capital and time per persona. A velvet nebula of fake profiles gains no weight without that costly record.
